x: All three are correct: about 58.6% of the landmass faces moderate-to-very-high earthquake risk, over 40 million ha (~12%) is flood-prone, and about 68% of the cultivable area is drought-vulnerable.

The Nepal flash floods of 26 August 2026 are a GLOF case: glacier retreat enlarges proglacial lakes that then burst; UNDP counts 26 GLOFs in Nepal since the 1970s. A tsunami, storm surge or urban drainage failure has nothing to do with a Himalayan flash flood.
Lower Assam is flood-prone (Brahmaputra plains), not drought-prone. The drought-prone regions listed are western Rajasthan, Kutch-Saurashtra, Marathwada-Vidarbha, interior Karnataka and Rayalaseema.

All three are correct: Tsunami Ready recognition uses 12 indicators, is renewable every 4 years, and India targets 100 villages (verified by the National Tsunami Ready Recognition Board under MoES, chaired by the Director, INCOIS).

All three pairs are correct: the territorial sea (12 nm) gives full sovereignty subject to innocent passage; the contiguous zone (24 nm) lets the state enforce customs, fiscal, immigration and sanitary laws; and the high seas carry freedom of navigation, overflight and research.

Statement 1 is correct: agroforestry grows trees with crops/livestock on the same land. Statement 2 is correct: the National Agroforestry Policy 2014 was India's first. Statement 3 is wrong: NFP 1988 is a forest policy (33% of area under forest overall, two-thirds in the hills, formal JFM); the first agroforestry policy came only in 2014. Hence 1 and 2 only.

IWMP dates to 2009-10, so A is correct. The others are mismatched: Hariyali is 2003 (not 2019), Jal Shakti Abhiyan is 2019 (not 2003), and the National River Conservation Plan is 1995 - 2014 is the year of Namami Gange.
